author: Ron Struthers
title: Beware The Bear
text:
This is a follow up to my July and October market observations.
Although there is not an official bear market in the major indexes, I believe we are already in one. A bear market is defined by a -20% decline or more versus a bull market by a +20% rise. I have been warning about this for several months, but nobody takes notice because they have been drinking at the punch bowl too long. The last bear market was about 10 years ago. Anyone remember?
I follow cycles closely, always looking for clues of continuation or change. I have been warning about a market top, but some recent changes smell a lot like a bear - the marijuana sector that has seen a lot of speculative money and has been in the bear status for some time; another speculative sector, cryptocurrencies, has been in a bear market all year and just sank lower. I warned on that cycle top last December.
The latest two signals are bonds and stock market leaders. The bond market shows signs of reversal, which means the economy is teetering and the cycle of rising interest rates is nearing an end. Perception took a dramatic shift in bonds. Speculators on U.S. futures markets slashed their bearish bets on 10-year Treasuries last week by the largest amount since April 2017, and the third largest since the Commodity Futures Trading Commission began compiling data in 1995. Time to look at my favorite charts that I have been using to predict and monitor these cycle changes. This is a 10-year treasury weekly chart and today we are above 119. I agree we will see some sort of a rally, but there is resistance around 121 and my old line in the sand at the 122 area. Last year I warned a drop below 122 and we would go much lower which we did. Now we would have to see a rise above 122 to convince me of any decent rally.
I do not believe the rally will be worth buying, like the 20-year treasury ETF ( TLT ). Nearing the end of the rising interest rate cycle is no surprise. I have been using this chart on Libor rates for the past year or so. It reveals that each interest rate cycle does not have to go as high to trigger an economic slow-down. This is chiefly because of rising debt levels in every cycle. Since my last update we have moved slightly above the trend line, so a peak in interest rates could be imminent. If the Fed relaxes, keep in mind that budget deficit pressure could still hold rates up.
Recessions are not confirmed until long after they have happened. I don't believe we are in or near a recession yet, but have definitely begun a slow-down.
U.S. retail sales slumped in September with a weak 0.1% rise and revised to -0.1% in the October report. Although October sales rebounded to 0.8%, a lot of that was building materials and autos because of Hurricane Florence. The start of the holiday buying binge is arriving this weekend and there is a lot of optimism for higher sales than last year. The next two months will give us a much better picture.
The stock market is also a leading indicator and it has not been painting a nice picture. It is not flashing a bright red warning sign yet, but has turned yellow. It just might be a matter of time before we enter the bear status. The tech leaders in the market have already done so.
The FANG stocks that have been leading the US indexes are in the bear territory:
Facebook ( FB ) is down about -39% from its August high.
Amazon ( AMZN ) is down about -27% from its September high.
Apple ( AAPL ) is down about -23% from its October high.
Netflix ( NFLX ) is down about -38% from its July high.
Alphabet ( GOOG ) is down about -26% from its July high.
I usually use a chart of the S&P 500 ( SPY ), but the NASDAQ Index or ETF ( QQQ ) paints perhaps a clearer picture. The drop to Tuesday's low was about -16% from the high so not official bear status. However, if the index drops below my 'line in the sand,' it will go lower and into an official bear market. The 200-day MA also looks to be turning down, another long-term negative. It is easier to see the potential head and shoulders top I have been commenting on, looking at the NASDAQ compared to S&P 500.
Another negative is oil prices. Oil hit my $75 to $80 target, but I believed it would eventually go higher to $100. We can throw that out the window now as the oil bull market ended last week. Support at $65 and $60 should have held, but with the break below $60 last week, it is official bear status. And prices are lower this week, hitting $53 yesterday.
Most metals and commodities are holding up well as I believe we are seeing some rotation into inflation hedges. Money coming out of the cyclical high equities is going into cash, bonds and a smaller bit in metals. The bright spot is gold, not that it is going a lot higher but is just bumping along sideways around a bottom. Once we get by the seasonal year-end weakness, prices should do better in late December or January. Some years the year-end weakness comes in November, so perhaps this trend of higher lows continues. That said, I would not be surprised to see a test again of the August low. I believe a break above $1240 will signal a move much higher. The large short positions will start covering above $1240 fueling further advances. Managed money increased its short position again in the recent dip to $1200.
Conclusion Can the Fed achieve a soft landing? Their track record is very poor so don't keep your hopes up. The odds are very high that the long equity bull market has ended. Markets are putting in topping patterns so will likely trade sideways for some time yet. Don't get stuck in the denial phase that will grow stronger. The famous 'it is different this time.' Any rallies should be used to lighten equity positions in stocks and equity funds. I would suggest higher levels in cash and now that we have seen a good correction in bonds, some allocation there is fine. I would be looking to buy defensive, high-paying, dividend stocks, like the ones I suggest in my Millennium index. I plan to dig up a few more of these, increase positions in metals and gold stocks. Marijuana is still a new and growing market, but the easy money is made. Selective positions in that sector can still do well.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
